notes:
Account context:
- Mid-market B2B SaaS (workflow/customer engagement). Product team owns evaluation; procurement/legal engaged for Dedicated.
- Started on Hosted API (self-serve -> demo -> 6-week POC). POC succeeded on quality but cost/per-token is main driver to move to Dedicated.
- CTO (Rohit Patel) and Head of Platform (Maya Lin) leading technical buy. VP Product (Elena Garcia) driving business case.
POC highlights / technical requirements:
- Workloads: conversational support-agent (multi-turn), semantic-search over product docs, in-app assistant for onboarding, summarization for release notes.
- Throughput target for Dedicated: sustained 35-60 reqs/sec (average request ~200 tokens), burst to 120 rps during daily peak.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 150ms, p90 < 350ms for standard chat flows; p99 target discussed at <= 800ms (customer wants tighter).
- Model preferences: open 7B/13B quantized variants for cost balance; option to fallback to 70B in edge cases (high-quality generation) but routed to higher-cost tier.
- Routing/fallback: need policy for model fallbacks by latency/cost tiers and region-aware routing (NA primary, EU for EU customers).
- Cost sensitivity: target to reduce per-token inference cost by ~40% vs hosted baseline via Dedicated + quantization + batching.
Procurement / Legal asks (current redlines):
- DPA: add EU data residency guarantee for EU user content, deletion windows, and standard SCCs.
- MSA: indemnity cap, limitation of liability tweaks, audit rights clause, SLA credit language tightened (customer requesting higher credits for downtime).
- Security: require KMS integration (bring-your-own-key), SOC2 Type II attestation, quarterly pen-test summary, and supplier subprocessor list.
- Onboarding deliverables: onboarding runbook, runbook for incident response, handoff to CSM for playbooks.
Customer quotes/notes from calls:
- "We liked the POC quality but cost is the blocker — need predictable bills and isolation for customer data." — Elena (VP Product).
- "SLA needs to include clear credits + 4h P1 response." — Maya (Head of Platform).
Actions taken by Redwood (sales/SE/legal):
- Hosted POC metrics and token breakdown provided (drive:/deals/beacontrail/poc-metrics.csv).
- SE (Priya) presented Dedicated sizing options: 4x A100-equivalent reserved nodes vs burst pool. Update pending.
- Legal (Redwood) responded to MSA/DPA redlines with comment set v1; awaiting counter from BeaconTrail legal.
- Security provided SOC2 package and network diagram; customer follow-up asks for KMS integration guide.
Open items / blockers:
- BeaconTrail legal pushed DPA redline on data residency and deletion timelines (needs explicit clause).
- SLA uptime: customer wants 99.99; Redwood proposing 99.95 + improved incident response. Negotiation in progress.
- Budget committee needs final ARR number; procurement will approve after legal signoff.
Next steps (short):
- AE (Alex) to send term sheet with final pricing and proposed SLA (target by 2026-03-17).
- SE (Priya) to validate Dedicated perf runbook and confirm capacity plan (by 2026-03-20).
- Legal exchange: BeaconTrail to send MSA/DPA counter by 2026-03-14; Redwood legal to prepare redline response.
